title: E2: hydroxide and 2-bromopropane
caption: One concerted step with ethanolic KOH and heat (in water, substitution competes). Hydroxide takes a β-hydrogen, the C–H bonding pair becomes the new π bond, and bromide leaves, all at once. The hydrogen and bromine are drawn on opposite sides (anti-periplanar), the arrangement E2 needs. Rate = k[R–X][base].
alt: E2 mechanism: hydroxide removes a hydrogen from the carbon next to the C–Br carbon while the C=C forms and bromide leaves, giving propene, water and bromide.
description: Left: 2-bromopropane with the bromine pointing up from carbon 2 and a hydrogen on carbon 1 pointing down, on the opposite side (anti-periplanar), and a hydroxide ion, drawn ⁻O–H with its lone pair facing that hydrogen. The conditions are KOH in ethanol, heated.
Three curly arrows act together: from a lone pair on hydroxide's oxygen to the hydrogen; from the C–H bond to between carbons 1 and 2, forming the π bond; and from the C–Br bond to the bromine.
Right: propene, water and a bromide ion.
